title: Introduce consent-driven KMS provisioner and RBAC v2 temporal grants
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Add a consent-driven KMS provisioning path that ties tenant-level consent events to ephemeral CMK leases and RBAC v2 temporal grants. This addresses compliance requests to ensure cryptographic keys used for customer workloads are provisioned only after an auditable consent event and that operator/service privileges to those keys are timebounded and revocable.

What this PR does: Implements a small service (kms-provisioner) that receives signed consent assertions, performs lightweight policy checks, mints ephemeral CMK grants via the KMS adapter, records a provenance envelope to the audit log, and issues RBAC v2 temporal grants to operator principals scoped to the key for the lease duration. The design favors clear auditability, conservative defaults (deny until consent), and operator observability.

Key behaviors and guarantees: - Consent assertions must be signed by an allowed consent issuer (tenant or delegated controller) and include a nonce and expiry. - Ephemeral CMK leases default to 1 hour and are configurable per-tenant policy. - RBAC temporal grants are encoded as role bindings with start/expiry timestamps and an auditable decision id. - All provisioning actions write an immutable audit envelope to the audit-writer with provenance headers and a hash of the consent assertion for dedupe. - Automatic revocation: if lease expires or consent is revoked, the provisioner triggers a revoke flow that removes RBAC temporal grants and requests KMS to revoke access.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind feature.consent_kms_provisioner (default off). Gradual rollout to internal tenants for 2 weeks, then to early enterprise customers with a migration runbook. We included a dry-run mode that simulates KMS calls and writes audit envelopes marked as simulated.

Testing and validation: unit tests for policy engine, integ tests with local KMS emulator, e2e exercise in benchmark-lab with a tenant fixture. CI includes static analysis, contract tests for the RBAC policy writer, and an audit-log ingestion smoke test.

Related work: Linear ENG-1734 (consent + key lifecycle), ENG-1810 (rbac temporal grants), and acks to previous residency/kms PRs for audit envelope formats.

Checklist: - [x] Service scaffolding and configs - [x] Policy engine + validation - [x] KMS adapter integration with lease+revoke - [x] RBAC v2 temporal grant writer - [x] Audit envelope producer - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Migration/runbook draft (docs/consent_kms_migration.md)

Notes: This change introduces no global default CMK creation; provisioning is tenant-triggered. The provisioner runs as a low-privilege operator and obtains a short-lived operator lease (separate from the tenant CMK lease) when performing KMS operations to reduce long-lived credentials exposure.

ci_details: Static analysis: pass; Unit: pass; Integration: pass (KMS emulator); Contract tests: pass; E2E dry-run: pass
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please clarify threat model for consent issuer compromise — can an attacker replay signed assertions? Consider enforcing one-time nonces and binding to request origin. (requested changes)
Maya Chen: Added nonce-store with TTL and included request origin binding in assertion validation. Also signaled dedupe by hashing assertion into audit envelope. Reply to Arjun. (resolved)
Sofia Martinez: Audit envelopes look good; add a metric for failed consent validations so SRE can alert on unusual rates. (requested changes)
Maya Chen: Added metrics + dashboard and alert for high failed-consent-rate. Updated observability/dashboards and alerts. (resolved)
Liam O'Connor: RBAC temporal grant revocation path needs to handle partial failures when KMS revoke succeeds but RBAC write fails; added retry/compensating logic and clearer logs. (approved)
Sofia Martinez: Approving after a quick smoke run in staging. (approved)
discussion_summary: Reviewers requested additional hardening around replay protection, observability for consent failures, and robust revoke semantics. The author implemented nonce-store, added metrics + alerts, and improved revoke retry/compensation logic. Staging smoke validated the happy path and simulated revocations.
security_review: security-team@redwood reviewed key handling and confirmed there are no long-lived operator secrets introduced; recommended KMS adapter run with an operator lease and for the provisioner to be deployed in a reserved namespace with a restricted RBAC role. Recommendations implemented.
performance_notes: Provisioner designed for async KMS ops; synchronous path only used during initial lease issuance. Benchmarked in benchmark-lab: median issuance latency 180ms (emulator), expected 300-500ms in managed KMS. Bulk provisioning uses batch consent mode (future work).
migration_notes: docs/consent_kms_migration.md includes operator runbook: enable feature flag, run dry-run to surface policy mismatches, migrate tenants via admin console, and monitor failed-consent-rate. A rollback path disables feature flag and revokes any ephemeral grants that were issued during rollout.
release_notes: Add consent-driven KMS provisioning and RBAC v2 temporal grants. Feature-flagged: feature.consent_kms_provisioner (default off). See docs/consent_kms_migration.md for migration steps.
merge_outcome: squash-merge by Sofia Martinez; commit message condensed to: 'kms-provisioner: consent-driven KMS lease provisioning + RBAC temporal grants (ENG-1734)'.
changelog_entry: Added kms-provisioner service which enables consent-driven ephemeral CMK provisioning and timebounded RBAC grants (feature-flagged).
notes_for_ops: Deploy in its own namespace with network policy restricting egress to KMS endpoints and audit-writer. Ensure KMS adapter credentials are bound to short operator leases. Monitor metrics: consent_requests, consent_failures, lease_issued, lease_revoked, rbac_grant_errors.
